agent_priors_used: Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): persistent caches and compiled workflows decay and require revalidation; maintenance/revalidation cost, not initial replay speed, usually determines whether work compression actually pays.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): an abstention gate calibrated on a disjoint split is required for a trustworthy false-accept rate; a signal that abstains on very few examples can obtain high unknown-precision trivially while retaining a high false-accept.
Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): single-vantage/network measurements over-generalize; external validity of an access-barrier schedule requires varying the source vantage (public IP/ASN/geography).

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a comparator that itself retains memory can erase an apparent treatment advantage; dynamic-range claims must survive a memoryful baseline, not only a memoryless one.
Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): small local models (3B-8B) commonly fail multi-step tool/Web-agent bars, so endpoint capability must be certified before any same-model benchmark against it.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a task bank pinned at ceiling (all arms succeed) or floor (all arms fail) cannot support a success/cost advantage; non-ceiling dynamic range is a prerequisite for a discriminating comparison.

allocation.question: Which materially different resolution architecture - (A) model-free structured slot/parameter binding with an explicit, independently checkable abstention condition, or (B) a retrieval/embedding resolver trained on independently authored goals - simultaneously reaches pooled_false_accept <= 0.10, coverage >= 0.50 and unknown_precision >= 0.85 on a disjoint calibration/test split AND retains the intact deterministic selection half (B-LEX-STRONG 97/113 = 0.8584) while generalizing its selection advantage to a held-out mechanism set and an independently curated synonym lexicon, thereby deciding whether resolve() ships as a deterministic resolver plus a valid abstention gate or must adopt the structured/retrieval architecture?
allocation.rationale: Decision counterfactual: a WIN licenses shipping resolve() as a deterministic resolver + calibrated abstention gate and unblocks the entity-resolution input to Product; a LOSS forces the structured/retrieval architecture and changes the Product integration; an INVALID (e.g., cannot power the FA<=0.10 test without an embedding stack) records an exact prerequisite and parks architecture B. Strongest fair baseline: the deterministic selection half that already passes (B-LEX-STRONG 0.8584) plus a retrieval/embedding resolver, and the trivial 'abstain-on-everything' baseline that trivially maximizes unknown-precision at zero coverage - coverage must stay >=0.50 for the gate to be meaningful. Validity/dependency: the calibrate/test split must be disjoint and the abstention threshold fixed on calibration only; the model-free arm is measurable now, the embedding arm needs a stack that is currently BLOCKED. Smallest decisive batch: enough test goals to power a pooled_false_accept<=0.10 comparison (target >=60 held-out goals spanning >=2 held-out mechanism families) with an independent synonym lexicon; bounded to first-party compute, no LLM endpoint. Stop/pivot trigger: if the split cannot be powered without the embedding stack, record the blocker and do not spend further cycles rediscovering it - park arm B and ship only if arm A passes.
